newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: ANYKSCHIU WINE 1Q SALES UP, PROFIT DOWN.
newsitem.headline: ANYKSCHIU WINE 1Q SALES UP, PROFIT DOWN.

text.p: Lithuanian wine and liqueur producer Anykschiu Wine said on Friday that its first quarter 1997 net profit dropped to 1.7 million litas from 3.9 million litas last year.

"Our net profit in the first quarter of this year was 1.7 million litas compared to the same period last year when our profit was 3.9 million litas," the company's director general, Jonas Makshtele, told Reuters.
"But our sales for the first three months of 1997 rose to 26 million litas compared with 21 million litas a year ago," Makshtele added.
Makshtele said that the company's net profit dropped because of an increase on excise duties on alcohol.
The company also has not been producing apple juice concentrate because of a lack of raw material.

"To preserve the present profit level in the second quarter of 1997 we will have to increase our sales since the government raised tariffs on alcohol again at the beginning of the month," Makshtele said.
The government decided to increase the excise duties on strong alcohol to 0.43 litas from 0.30 litas for every percent of alcohol in the bewerage litre.
"Liqueur makes 25-30 percent of our production and it is likely that we will get no profit from its production in the first quarter," Makshtele said.
Makshtele said he expected profit from the wine sales where the excise duty was raised to 0.17 litas from 0.15 litas for every percent of alcohol in the litre.
The company is 84.5 percent state owned and is not slated for privatisation before the year 2000.
The company is listed on the A group of the Vilnius bourse.
